title: secrets: a report-only check for stored `secret:` references that more than one holder names, or that a column other than the one that minted it holds
body:
domain:server#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F

Follow-up of #27582 (PR #27695), from its contract review record `6507826814` (should-fix S1). Rule level only.

## What is missing

#27695 makes a non-system write keep only its own record's `secret:` reference. Values stored before that change are not re-examined (the PR says so). The existing report, `os secret orphans` (`sys-secret-orphan-report.ts`, `secret-reference-union.ts`), classifies handles that NOTHING names; it does not answer whether a handle is named by more than one holder, or held by a column other than the one whose namespace/key it carries. `releaseSecretHandles` asks the namespace/key question only when it releases.

## Wanted

A report-only extension of the orphan report (no automatic repair, no deletion), listing each `sys_secret` handle that is named by more than one record/column, or whose holder column is not the column its namespace/key name, with counts and the holder object/field (never the secret, never the handle's plaintext). Note: a predicate update can legitimately share one handle across the rows it matched (#27495); the report must say how it tells that case apart or list it separately. Whether a repair path follows is a later decision.

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's.
